text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An editorial criticises Prime Minister Fatos Nano's coalition government for failing to convince Italian authorities not to turn back some 15,000 Albanian refugees who fled the country amid violence and anarchy in March.
- We are determined to get rid of all corrupt policemen, the deputy interior minister Ndre Legisi said in interview.
- Parliament speaker Skender Gjinushi said a referendum on the new constitution would be held on February 15.
- Interior Minister Neritan Ceka has reiterated an appeal on some 4,000 supporters of Democratic Party of former President Sali Berisha to hand in weapons.
- The paper says several state and private banks operate without new licences.
- Finance Ministry has invited six foreign administrators to audit investment companies in line with International Monetary Fund's recommendations on transparency of investment schemes.
- Special police forces crackdown on criminal gangs in the port town of Vlore.
- Six people wanted by police for rape and robbery were killed in an ambush by a rival gang near the southern town of Kucove on Monday.
- An IMF delegation arrived in Albania to discuss the transparency on investment companies with the finance ministry.
- Special police forces detained over 50 people in the southern town of Vlore for alleged links with criminal gangs.
- The opposition Democratic Party accuses Interior Minister Neritan Ceka of turning a blind eye on criminal gangs spreading terror in southern Albania.
